title: Grove's 'credit platform' operates in practice as a diversified allocator across tokenized credit, DeFi lending, AMM liquidity and stablecoin conversion
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.1.2.1 lists Grove's Active Allocation System Instances on Ethereum Mainnet under fifteen protocol headings, and the mix is broader than the mandate language of A.6.1.1.2.1 suggests.

Four distinct exposure types appear. **Tokenized credit and treasuries**: Centrifuge (JTRSY, JAAA, ACRDX), BlackRock BUIDL-I, Superstate USTB, Securitize's Tokenized AAA CLO Fund, Galaxy Arch CLOs and Galaxy Warehouse, Maple syrupUSDC. **Crypto-native yield**: Ethena USDe, sUSDe and the Pendle-style PT-USDe / PT-sUSDe principal tokens. **DeFi lending**: Aave Core v3 and Aave Horizon, and a large set of Morpho vaults. **Market infrastructure**: Curve and Uniswap pools, plus direct positions in issuer stablecoins RLUSD (Ripple) and AUSD (Agora), and a Paxos USDC-to-USDG conversion route.

The presence of Ethena principal tokens alongside AAA CLO funds is the notable spread. These sit at opposite ends of the risk spectrum — one is a duration-stripped claim on a synthetic-dollar basis trade, the other is senior structured credit — and both are held under the same Primitive with the same governance treatment.

The practical reading is that "institutional-grade credit platform" describes the **counterparty standard and the distribution ambition**, not a narrow asset class. Grove's actual book is a cross-sector stablecoin allocator, which is why the Core Council Risk Advisor gate (A.6.1.1.2.2.2.2.2.1.2.4) attaches to this Primitive specifically rather than to the Agent as a whole.
description: Fifteen protocol directories on Ethereum Mainnet alone span CLO funds, treasury tokens, lending markets, LP positions and issuer mint routes — far wider than credit origination.
